claims.value: Napoleon’s July note describes the Aragon corps at 13,000; this is a regional corps estimate during the first siege, not an opening assault count.
claims.rationale: The full page’s recap identifies the Aragon corps, alongside other regional corps. No complete local French return was inspected. English rendering (ours): "that of Aragon, 13,000."

claims.value: Toreno says Verdier brought reinforcements and replaced Lefebvre in chief command because of higher rank.
claims.rationale: The earlier Lefebvre period is retained; Bodart’s Verdier label is not extended backwards automatically. English rendering (ours): "General Verdier brought them and, by higher rank, replaced Lefebvre in chief command."

claims.value: Toreno records Palafox withdrawing to seek forces while Zaragoza’s initial defence continued.
claims.rationale: Army-level authority and physical presence differ; the page places this in the initial June episode. English rendering (ours): "Palafox, seeing how superior the enemy numbers were, decided to withdraw and passed in order to Longares."

claims.value: Calvo de Rozas released San Genis, who then laid out fortification works with the Tabuenca architects.
claims.rationale: Specific engineering and civil authority, not universal credit for all listed officers. English rendering (ours): "He was released only by Calvo de Rozas’s order on the morning of the 16th; San Genis then promptly laid out several fortification works."

claims.value: Napoleon’s July note assigns side A 10,600 to the camp before Zaragoza, distinct from the total 13,000 in Aragon and Navarre including garrison, mobile column and artillery.
claims.rationale: Local camp versus regional population, not the June opening muster. English rendering (ours): "At this moment in Aragon and Navarre: Zaragoza camp 10,600; Pamplona garrison 800; Pamplona mobile column 1,400; artillery 200; total 13,000."

open_questions: Recover dated opening and later garrison/besieger returns and the Lefebvre-to-Verdier command transition, using the siege journals and Palafox papers.
Deferred: the dated original returns and reports identified above, and any deeper source-lineage reconciliation. No additional research cycle follows merely from this gap.

Source dependence: Bodart is a later compilation. Toreno, Foy, Oman, Saint-Cyr and the official Correspondance are interested or retrospective source families, and embedded/reprinted reports are not extra independent witnesses. Agreement does not establish independence.

A.strength_population_and_time: Bodart’s engagement-level available force has no opening muster date. Napoleon’s 14 July note distinguishes 10,600 in the Zaragoza camp from 13,000 in the Aragon/Navarre command; neither resolves the opening strength or all later employment.
A.command_scope: Printed side-A commander Verdier; local/superior authority and transitions remain limited to the additional passages cited below. Toreno says Verdier brought reinforcements and replaced Lefebvre in chief command because of higher rank.
A.army_continuity: Unknown: these passages do not establish a cross-engagement army identity.

B.strength_population_and_time: Bodart’s engagement-level available force; no dated opening return. Civilians, recruits, regular troops and surrender survivors are not interchangeable. Alternatives/limits: The checked Spanish passages do not give a comparable dated opening garrison return; Bodart’s recruits/armed inhabitants remain a separate compilation population.
B.command_scope: Printed side-B commander Palafox; local/superior authority and transitions remain limited to the additional passages cited below. Toreno records Palafox withdrawing to seek forces while Zaragoza’s initial defence continued. Calvo de Rozas released San Genis, who then laid out fortification works with the Tabuenca architects.
B.army_continuity: Unknown: repeated names and formation labels do not establish continuity.
